chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bought a sheep and then wanted to buy one fatter than it, he said: 'He buys the new one, and when he buys it, he sells the first one.' And I do not know if he meant a sheep, he said: or a cow. And the limit of leanness that is not acceptable in sacrificial animals is that there be no fat on its kidney. He narrated that.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper procedure for upgrading a sacrificial animal and what defines an unacceptable level of leanness?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to ensure the validity of the udhiyah by preventing the sale of a substandard animal before securing a superior replacement, thereby avoiding accidental disposal of the sacrifice. The hadith further clarifies the specific physical defect (huzal) that invalidates the animal, defining it as the absence of fat on the kidneys, a criterion rooted in the practical assessment of the animal's health and maturity.
